tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

severity.description: Set when the review instructions ask for it. important: a bug the change adds or makes worse; pre_existing: a bug that was there before the change; nit: a minor issue

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

(If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

# SOLLUX landing page

A static landing page for SOLLUX, built from a Figma design as a recruitment task. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework and no build step.

## Running it

- Open `index.html` directly in a browser (works over `file://`), or serve the folder with any static server.
- All paths are relative, so the site also works from a GitHub Pages subfolder.

Node is only needed for development tooling (`npm install` first):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run assets` | Rebuilds optimised images, icons and fonts from `assets/raw/` |
| `npm run lint` | Stylelint, html-validate and a Prettier check |
| `npm run format` | Formats the code with Prettier |
| `npm test` | Playwright tests (added once the page is complete) |

"Wpsółpraca" in Figma is a typo; the page uses "Współpraca" (NOTES.md). ### 3.9 Polish pass - Favicon; html-validate, Stylelint and Prettier clean. - Check the 320–1920 range by hand; Lighthouse sanity check. ## 4. Acceptance criteria (Playwright tests, written after the page is built) 1. **Slider timing** (`page.clock`): the slide changes at 3 s; the crossfade finishes by 600 ms; the progress bar is `scaleX(1)` at 3 s and resets after the change; it pauses on hover; prev/next and segment clicks work. 2. **Header hover:** after 250 ms the computed `color` is black and the overlay opacity is 1; both revert on leave. 3. **Tile hover:** after the transition the image transform is `scale(1.1)` and the button overlay opacity is 1. 4. **Burger menu** (< 1280 px): opens and closes, `aria-expanded` toggles, Esc closes, focus is trapped and returns to the burger. 5. **Lamps:** - a click toggles `aria-pressed` and the glow opacity on both slides; - lamp boxes stay aligned with their reference positions in the stage (tolerance in px, agreed once measured) at 375 / 768 / 1440 / 1920; - at 375 the lamps are inside the viewport and don't overlap the hero text box. 6. **Shader:** - the canvas has a WebGL context and draws non-blank pixels; - with WebGL disabled (via `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext` override in `addInitScript`) the `.shader--static` fallback is shown and there are no errors. 7. **Accessibility:** axe finds no violations on the full page (desktop and mobile). 8. **No horizontal scroll** at widths from 320 to 1920 (stepped): `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`. 9. **No console errors or failed requests** on load, also when opened over `file://`. 10. **Reduced motion** (`emulateMedia`): no autoplay, the shader doesn't animate (static fallback), no transform transitions (tile zoom, slide scale-in, menu slide). Opacity fades are allowed. 11. **Touch:** with `hasTouch` and no hover capability, tapping a tile or the header leaves no stuck hover state. 12. **Lighthouse (mobile)** on the deployed GitHub Pages URL: **≥ 90** in Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO. - `noindex` is intentional; if SEO flags it, note it and keep the meta tag. # SOLLUX landing page

A static landing page for SOLLUX, built from a Figma design as a recruitment task. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework and no build step.

## Running it

- Open `index.html` directly in a browser (works over `file://`), or serve the folder with any static server.
- All paths are relative, so the site also works from a GitHub Pages subfolder.

Node is only needed for development tooling (`npm install` first):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run assets` | Rebuilds optimised images, icons and fonts from `assets/raw/` |
| `npm run lint` | Stylelint, html-validate and a Prettier check |
| `npm run format` | Formats the code with Prettier |
| `npm test` | Playwright tests (added once the page is complete) |

## Deviations from the design

The full list of decisions is in [`design/NOTES.md`](design/NOTES.md). The ones a reviewer would notice:

- **Copy fixes:** the SOLLUX SMART tile button says "Pobierz aplikację na telefon" (the design has "aplikacje"), and the footer column is "Współpraca" (the design has "Wpsółpraca").
- **Contrast:** THORO and Konfigurator tiles have a subtle dark gradient behind their white text, so the text meets WCAG contrast (4.5:1 for the eyebrow, 3:1 for the title). The design colours are unchanged.
- **Hero lamps:** in the design the lamps are part of the rock photo. Slide 1 uses a copy of that photo with the lamps removed (an AI edit; it re-rendered the rock slightly, see NOTES.md), so the lamps are separate images that stay put on both slides while only the backgrounds crossfade and zoom.
- **Lamp light (the creative part of the brief):** click a lamp (or Tab to it and press Enter) to switch it on: a short flicker, a warm diffuser glow, a light cone and light on the rock, while the room dims a little. A "Kliknij lampę" hint shows on the first visit. Turn on all three for a small surprise in the headline. With a mouse, the lamps also drift slightly with the cursor (the nearest one most); off on touch screens and with reduced motion.
- **Mobile:** there are no mobile designs. The header switches to a burger menu below 1280 px, the tiles go to one column below 1024 px, and the benefits use two columns on phones.
- **Hero slider:** autoplay pauses while the arrows or progress bar are hovered or keyboard focus is inside the hero, and there's a pause/play button next to the progress bar (WCAG 2.2.2).

new='''## 4. Acceptance criteria (Playwright tests)

The suite is in `tests/`, one spec file per area; `npm test` runs it (setup in README). Criteria 1–11 and the lamp light and parallax are covered; criterion 12 is run after the deploy.

1. **Slider timing** (`slider.spec.js`, `page.clock` paused before load): the slide changes at 3 s; the crossfade finishes by 600 ms; the progress bar is nearly full just before 3 s and resets after the change; it pauses while the mouse is over a control and with the pause button; prev/next and segment clicks work and restart the 3 s timer.
2. **Header hover** (`header.spec.js`): after the transition the computed `color` is the ink colour and the overlay (`::before`) opacity is 1; both revert on leave.
3. **Tile hover** (`tiles.spec.js`): after the transition the image's `scale` property is 1.1 (the zoom uses `scale`, not `transform`) and the button overlay opacity is 1, on all four tiles.
4. **Burger menu** (`header.spec.js`, at 768): opens and closes, `aria-expanded` toggles, the rest of the page is `inert`, Esc closes, focus is trapped and returns to the burger.
5. **Lamps** (`lamps.spec.js`):
   - a click toggles `aria-pressed` and the glow opacity on both slides; Enter and Space work too;
   - lamp boxes stay within **1 px** (user-approved; measured max 0.016 px) of their reference positions in the stage at 375 / 768 / 1440 / 1920;
   - at 375 the lamps are inside the viewport and don't overlap the hero text box.
6. **Lamp light** (`lamps.spec.js`):
   - the room dims a little more with each lamp (`--lamp-dim-1/2/3`), not at all with none, and the blended light layer is hidden again once nothing is lit;
   - with all three lamps on, "w nowym świetle" glows (easter egg); it goes off when one is switched off; the H1 is still read once;
   - the first-visit hint goes after the first click and stays gone after a reload.
7. **Lamp parallax** (`parallax.spec.js`):
   - with the cursor at the hero's edge each lamp moves by 12 px × its depth (at 1920), its glow and cone move with it and its rock pool moves 0.3 of that;
   - when the cursor leaves the hero the lamps ease back to rest: same positions as before, no inline properties, no `.hero--parallax`;
   - nothing moves on touch (`hasTouch`) or under reduced motion.
8. **Shader** (`shader.spec.js`):
   - the canvas has a WebGL context and draws non-blank pixels that change over time;
   - with WebGL disabled (`HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext` override in `addInitScript`) the section never gets `.shader--ready`, the canvas stays at opacity 0, the CSS gradient shows and there are no errors.
9. **Accessibility** (`a11y.spec.js`): axe finds no violations on the full page (desktop and mobile).
10. **No horizontal scroll** (`layout.spec.js`) at widths from 320 to 1920 (stepped): `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`.
11. **No console errors or failed requests** (`console.spec.js`) on load and while scrolling, over http and over `file://`.
12. **Reduced motion** (`reduced-motion.spec.js`, `emulateMedia`): no autoplay and no pause button, the shader shows a still frame, no transform transitions (tile zoom, slide scale-in, menu slide). Opacity fades are allowed.
13. **Touch** (`touch.spec.js`): with `hasTouch` and no hover capability, tapping a tile or the header leaves no stuck hover state.
14. **Lighthouse (mobile)**, after the deploy, on the GitHub Pages URL: **≥ 90** in Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO.
    - `noindex` is intentional; if SEO flags it, note it and keep the meta tag. Don't remove it to pass.
    - Also check the font timing there (the font preload was removed, §2).
    - Run by hand or with Lighthouse CLI (needs approval as a new dependency).

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "criterion 1[0-2]\|criteria 1\|criterion [5-9]" PLAN.md README.md NOTES.md design/NOTES.md CLAUDE.md tests/*.js 2>/dev/null; grep -n "^## " PLAN.md

---
name: reviewer
description: Read-only code reviewer for the SOLLUX landing page. Reviews the code against CLAUDE.md and PLAN.md with fresh context and reports findings with file:line and severity. Never edits anything.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---

You are an independent reviewer of a static landing page (plain HTML, CSS and JS, no build step). You did not write this code. Review it with fresh eyes and report; you never edit, create or delete files.

## Read first
1. `CLAUDE.md`: the working rules (stack, paths, BEM, tokens, motion, assets, workflow).
2. `PLAN.md`: the build plan, section decisions and acceptance criteria (§4).
3. `design/NOTES.md`: decisions that override the spec. A deviation recorded there is not a finding.

## Then review
- `index.html`, `css/*.css`, `js/*.js`, and `tests/*.js` with `playwright.config.js` (do the tests really check what PLAN.md §4 says they check?).
- Skip `assets/`, `design/figma/`, `node_modules/`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`.

Check in particular:
- **CLAUDE.md rules:** relative paths only (no leading `/`); classic `<script defer>`, no ES modules in the site; BEM names; JS hooks via `data-*`, not classes; colours and durations as tokens from `css/tokens.css`, not hard-coded; one easing; only `transform`/`opacity` animated (plus the header `color` exception); hover effects inside `@media (hover: hover)` with `:focus-visible` equivalents; `prefers-reduced-motion` handled; links `href="#"`; the search form doesn't submit; semantic HTML, real buttons, alt text.
- **Correctness:** JS bugs, race conditions, listeners or rAF loops that never stop, missing null checks for elements the script assumes, behaviour that breaks over `file://`.
- **Accessibility:** focus order, focus visibility, ARIA state that can go out of sync, keyboard traps, contrast notes.
- **Performance:** image `srcset`/`sizes` and `loading`, layout thrash, unnecessary work while off-screen.
- **Plan drift:** places where the code and PLAN.md disagree. Say which one looks right.
- **Dead code:** unused selectors, tokens, functions or files.

## Rules
- Verify every finding by reading the code. Cite exact `path:line`. No guesses: if you're unsure, say so and mark it "uncertain".
- Don't report style preferences that Prettier or Stylelint already settle.
- Don't propose large rewrites; describe the smallest fix.

## Report format
A list, most severe first. For each finding:
- **Severity:** high (broken behaviour, a CLAUDE.md rule broken, an a11y failure), medium (likely bug or real inconsistency), low (cleanup, nit).
- **Where:** `path:line`
- **Finding:** what is wrong, in one or two sentences.
- **Evidence:** the rule or code that shows it.
- **Suggested fix:** the smallest change.

End with a short list of what you checked and found fine.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\user\OneDrive\Документы\idomods-task\.claude\skills\web-design-guidelines

# Web Interface Guidelines

Review files for compliance with Web Interface Guidelines.

## How It Works

1. Read the bundled guidelines at [references/command.md](references/command.md)
2. Read the specified files (or prompt user for files/pattern)
3. Check against all rules in the guidelines
4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

## Guidelines Source

The rules are bundled with this skill in the [references/command.md](references/command.md) file. Read that file before each review. Do not fetch rules from the network.

The snapshot is pinned to a specific upstream commit:

Source: https://github.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/blob/434b7f91364665f2f733b310ec54809bf8f37937/command.md

SHA-256: `d246b026f4f29b5823a9cc857f9edf3d2507002e055e32040cadeaf3b38e0234`

The file contains all the rules and output format instructions.
Where it says `index.html css/`, use the files or pattern the user asked to review.

## Updating the Guidelines

To update the snapshot to a newer upstream version:

1. Get the latest commit SHA: `gh api repos/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/commits/main --jq .sha`
2. Download it: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/<SHA>/command.md -o references/command.md`
3. Review the changes, then update the Source URL and SHA-256 above (`shasum -a 256 references/command.md`)
4. Regenerate `skills/web-design-guidelines.zip` so it matches the updated folder

## Usage

When a user provides a file or pattern argument:
1. Read [references/command.md](references/command.md)
2. Read the specified files
3. Apply all rules from the guidelines
4. Output findings using the format specified in the guidelines

If no files specified, ask the user which files to review.

Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  ## Review report: SOLLUX landing page (read-only; only Read, Grep and Glob were used)
  
  Findings are listed most severe first. Severities follow the rubric in `.claude/agents/reviewer.md`, where any broken CLAUDE.md rule counts as **high**. Findings 1 to 3 are high only for that reason. Their real impact is small.
  
  ---
  
  **1. High: colours hard-coded outside `tokens.css`**
  - **Where:**
    - `css/lamps.css:150-151, 236-238, 265-267, 281-283, 381-382`
    - `css/hero.css:54, 59, 316`
    - `css/tiles.css:96-97`
    - `css/shader.css:19`
  - **Finding:** Raw `rgb()` and hex colours are used in component CSS. Two related tokens, `--c-light-amber` and `--c-light-ember` (`tokens.css:27-28`), are never used. Their values (255 180 100 and 255 150 70) are typed out by hand at `lamps.css:281-282`.
  - **Evidence:** CLAUDE.md says: "Design tokens are CSS custom properties in `css/tokens.css`. Don't hard-code colours … elsewhere."
    - `hero.css:54` has `--hero-sky: #9c6744;` and `hero.css:59` has `#c5afa3`.
    - `rgb(16 16 17 / …)` in hero, tiles and shader is `--c-black` with alpha.
  - **Suggested fix:**
    - Move the sky colours and the light-gradient stops into `tokens.css`.
    - Write the alpha variants as `color-mix(in srgb, var(--c-black) var(--scrim), transparent)` and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--c-light-amber) 90%, transparent)`, and so on.
    - Then either use `--c-light-amber` and `--c-light-ember` or delete them.
  
  **2. High: durations hard-coded outside `tokens.css`**
  - **Where:** `css/lamps.css:316` (`1.2s` delay), `css/lamps.css:337` (`1.6s` pulse); also `js/lamp-parallax.js:20` (`SMOOTH_MS = 160`).
  - **Finding:** The hint's entry delay and pulse period are literals. In JS the parallax time constant is a literal too, even though `hero-slider.js:35` shows the existing pattern of reading durations from CSS.
  - **Evidence:** CLAUDE.md says: "Don't hard-code colours or durations elsewhere."
  - **Suggested fix:** Add `--dur-hint-delay` and `--dur-hint-pulse` to `tokens.css` and use them. The JS constant is uncertain, since it's a smoothing constant rather than a transition. Read it from CSS or leave it with a comment.
  
  **3. High: hover effects with no `:focus-visible` equivalent**
  - **Where:** `css/hero.css:199-203` (the arrow overlay is hover only), `css/footer.css:34-39` (the footer link underline is hover only).
  - **Finding:** Keyboard users get the global focus ring but not the hover state. Everywhere else (buttons, tiles, header, lamp peek) mirrors hover with `:focus-visible`.
  - **Evidence:** CLAUDE.md says: "Keyboard users get the same states through `:focus-visible` / `:focus-within`."
  - **Suggested fix:** Add `.hero__arrow:focus-visible::before { opacity: 1; }` and `.footer__link:focus-visible { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 3px; }`, outside the hover media query.
  
  **4. Medium: no favicon (plan drift, Lighthouse risk)**
  - **Where:** `index.html:3-43` (no `<link rel="icon">`). `favicon.svg` doesn't exist at the repo root.
  - **Finding:** PLAN §1, §2 and §3.9 list `favicon.svg` ("the 'S' from `union.svg`"). Without it, browsers request `/favicon.ico` from the domain root. On a GitHub Pages project subfolder that returns 404.
  - **Uncertain:** whether Chrome logs that 404 to the console, which would hurt Lighthouse Best Practices (criterion 12). `console.spec.js` wouldn't catch it, because headless Chromium doesn't normally request favicons.
  - **Suggested fix:** Add `favicon.svg` and `<link rel="icon" href="favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">`, using a relative path.
  
  **5. Medium (uncertain): white hero and header text on slide 2 has no scrim on desktop**
  - **Where:** `css/hero.css:58-61`; the scrim is only applied inside `@media (max-aspect-ratio: 5/4)` at `hero.css:311-317`.
  - **Finding:** PLAN §3.3 says white on the interior photo's sky (`#c5afa3`) is about 2.1:1, so a 45% scrim was added, but only in contained (portrait) mode. In landscape cover mode, the white header links (14 px), eyebrow, H1 and badge sit directly on the interior photo.
  - **Evidence:** axe can't measure text on images, so `a11y.spec.js` can't catch this. I didn't open the raw photo (`assets/` is out of scope), so I couldn't measure it.
  - **Suggested fix:** Measure the contrast on slide 2 at 1280 and 1920. If it's under 4.5:1, apply a text-side scrim like `.tile--scrim` in landscape mode as well.
  
  **6. Low: easter-egg fade uses the zoom token, so reduced motion removes the fade**
  - **Where:** `css/lamps.css:386`, together with `css/tokens.css:99`.
  - **Finding:** `.hero__glow::after` uses `transition: opacity var(--dur-zoom)`. Under reduced motion, `--dur-zoom` is 0 ms, so this opacity fade (which is allowed) snaps instead.
  - **Suggested fix:** Use `var(--dur-fade)`.
  
  **7. Low: hero `sizes` and preload `imagesizes` ignore the hero's height clamp and use `vh`, not `svh`**
  - **Where:** `index.html:24`, `index.html:249`, `index.html:276`.
  - **Finding:** `(max-aspect-ratio: 16/9) calc(100vh * 1.7778)` doesn't match the real stage width, `max(100%, clamp(560px, 100svh, 1080px) * 16/9)`.
    - It underestimates on short landscape viewports. At 800 × 520 the real stage is about 995 px, but `sizes` gives 924.
    - It overestimates above 1080 px of height.
    - PLAN §2 specifies `svh`.
  - **Suggested fix:** Use `calc(clamp(560px, 100svh, 1080px) * 1.7778)` in all three, keeping them identical so the preload is still reused.
  
  **8. Low (uncertain): first-visit hint pulses forever, and the lamp flicker frequency**
  - **Where:** `css/lamps.css:337` (`hint-pulse … infinite`), `css/lamps.css:192-227` (450 ms flicker).
  - **Finding, pulse:** The pulsing dot repeats indefinitely until the first lamp click, with no way to stop it except reduced motion. This may fall under WCAG 2.2.2 (blinking content longer than 5 s).
  - **Finding, flicker:** It has about 3 opacity peaks in 450 ms. Whether this crosses the 2.3.1 flash threshold depends on the lit area and luminance change, which I can't verify statically.
  - **Suggested fix:** Limit the pulse, e.g. `animation-iteration-count: 3`. Visually check the flicker with all lamps lit at 1920.
  
  **9. Low: closing the menu via a link leaves focus on a hidden element**
  - **Where:** `js/header.js:66-68`.
  - **Finding:** `close(false)` doesn't move focus. After the slide-out, the focused panel link becomes `visibility: hidden`, so a keyboard user loses their place.
  - **Suggested fix:** Call `close(true)`, or move focus to the burger when the menu closes while focus is inside it.
  
  **10. Low (uncertain): lamp hit boxes overlap**
  - **Where:** `index.html:298`, `316`, `334`.
  - **Finding:** The lamp buttons are full image rectangles, transparent corners included. Computed from the inline `--x/--y/--w` values and the image aspect ratios:
    - lamp 3 (later in the DOM, so on top) covers lamp 1 at about x 39.6–43.8 %, y 40.2–46.7 % of the stage;
    - lamp 2 covers lamp 1 at about x 56.0–59.0 %, y 30.7–46.7 %.
    
    Whether this overlap covers any of lamp 1's visible pixels is uncertain.
  - **Suggested fix:** Check by clicking. If needed, trim the hit area with a `clip-path` polygon on `.lamp`.
  
  **11. Low: parallax does work on every mouse move anywhere on the page**
  - **Where:** `js/lamp-parallax.js:113-121`, `js/lamp-parallax.js:92-96`.
  - **Finding:** A document-wide `pointermove` wakes a rAF tick that reads two bounding rects, even when the cursor is over the footer. It settles in one frame, so the cost is small.
  - **Suggested fix:** In the handler, skip `wake()` when `atRest` and the pointer is outside the last known hero rect, which is already refreshed on scroll.
  
  **12. Low: tests check less than PLAN §4 says**
  - `tests/header.spec.js:43,48`: only `main` is checked for `inert`. PLAN says "the rest of the page"; the footer and skip link aren't checked.
  - `tests/slider.spec.js:69-77`: the timer restart is tested only for "next". PLAN says prev, next and segment clicks restart the 3 s timer.
  - `tests/lamps.spec.js:131-141`: "in view" is checked only horizontally; there's no `b.y + b.height <= 812` check.
  - `tests/reduced-motion.spec.js:11-17`: `movingAnimations` only looks at CSS transitions, not keyframe animations. The hint is also hidden by default (`tests/helpers.js:5-13`), so removing `hint-pulse` under reduced motion is never tested.
  - **Suggested fix:** Add the missing assertions; none of them needs a snapshot or a threshold change.
  
  **13. Low: PLAN.md is out of date (the code looks right in each case)**
  - PLAN §1 lists `js/menu.js`; the menu lives in `js/header.js`.
  - PLAN §3.1 has `--gutter: clamp(16px, 8.33vw, 160px)`; `tokens.css:83` has `16px`, which is consistent with PLAN §3.2.
  - PLAN §3.3 describes centring with `translateX(calc(-50% + var(--stage-x)))`; `hero.css:66-73` uses `top/left: 50%` + `translate(-50%, -50%)`.
  - The PLAN §2 `imagesizes` text has no contained-mode entry.
  - **Suggested fix:** Update PLAN.md.
  
  **14. Low: dead code**
  - `tokens.css:27-28`: `--c-light-amber` and `--c-light-ember` are unused (see finding 1).
  - `js/shader.js:147`: the `data-render-scale` override is never used by the markup or the tests.
  - `css/hero.css:269-271` (`.hero__pause[hidden]`) and `css/lamps.css:319-321` (`.hero__hint[hidden]`) repeat `base.css:87-89` (`[hidden] { display: none !important }`).
  - **Suggested fix:** Remove them, or keep `data-render-scale` with a test that uses it.
  
  ---
  
  ### Checked and found fine
  - **Paths and loading:** only relative paths (no leading `/` in any href, src, srcset or `url()`); classic `<script defer>`, no modules, every script an IIFE with a `DOMContentLoaded` guard; works over file:// (no font preload, `localStorage` in try/catch).
  - **Copy and controls:** every link is `href="#"`; the search form's `submit` is prevented (`header.js:13-18`).
  - **Class names and hooks:** BEM names throughout (Stylelint pattern too); JS hooks are all `data-*`, and classes are only toggled for state.
  - **Motion:**
    - one easing token, with `--ease-out` only for scale-ups and zoom;
    - only `transform`, `scale`, `translate` and `opacity` animate, plus the header `color` exception and discrete `visibility`;
    - hover rules sit inside `(hover: hover)` (apart from finding 3);
    - reduced motion is handled: tokens neutralise scale and movement, there's no autoplay, the pause button is hidden, the shader draws one frame, parallax is off, the flicker becomes a fade and the panel only fades.
  - **JS lifecycle:**
    - The slider, shader and parallax rAF loops all stop: on pause, on hidden tab or off-screen, or once settled.
    - The slider clamps time gaps; the progress bar and the slide change share one clock.
    - Shader: context lost/restored, no-WebGL fallback, debounced ResizeObserver, 60 fps cap.
    - Null checks for every queried element. One exception, harmless in this markup: `hero-slider.js` assumes prev/next exist whenever there are 2+ slides.
  - **Accessibility:**
    - Burger: `aria-expanded`, everything outside the header `inert`, focus trap, Esc returns focus, closes when widening past 1280.
    - Slider ARIA: roledescription, "1 z 2" labels, `aria-hidden` on the inactive slide, `aria-current` on the active segment, pause button `aria-pressed`.
    - Lamps: `aria-pressed` with a constant label; the hint is `aria-hidden`; the easter-egg copy is hidden from assistive tech via `content: … / ''`.
    - A visible two-tone focus ring on both light and dark backgrounds; alt text on content images and `alt=""` on decorative ones; real buttons for every control.
  - **Images:** tile `srcset`/`sizes` match PLAN §3.6; `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"` on everything below the fold; hero slide 1 has `fetchpriority="high"` and its `sizes` match the preload `imagesizes` exactly.
  - **Layout and performance:** the hero stage height comes only from `aspect-ratio`, as PLAN requires; `will-change` is set only while the parallax moves.
  - **Tests:** the suite maps to criteria 1–11, and the assertions check what they claim (e.g. the reduced-motion burger test does catch a slide transition). No snapshots or loosened thresholds.
  - **Dependencies:** `package.json` devDependencies match the list in CLAUDE.md.

- **Finding, pulse:** The pulsing dot repeats indefinitely until the first lamp click, with no way to stop it except reduced motion. This may fall under WCAG 2.2.2 (blinking content longer than 5 s).
- **Finding, flicker:** It has about 3 opacity peaks in 450 ms. Whether this crosses the 2.3.1 flash threshold depends on the lit area and luminance change, which I can't verify statically.
- **Suggested fix:** Limit the pulse, e.g. `animation-iteration-count: 3`. Visually check the flicker with all lamps lit at 1920.

**9. Low: closing the menu via a link leaves focus on a hidden element**
- **Where:** `js/header.js:66-68`.
- **Finding:** `close(false)` doesn't move focus. After the slide-out, the focused panel link becomes `visibility: hidden`, so a keyboard user loses their place.
- **Suggested fix:** Call `close(true)`, or move focus to the burger when the menu closes while focus is inside it.

**10. Low (uncertain): lamp hit boxes overlap**
- **Where:** `index.html:298`, `316`, `334`.
- **Finding:** The lamp buttons are full image rectangles, transparent corners included. Computed from the inline `--x/--y/--w` values and the image aspect ratios:
  - lamp 3 (later in the DOM, so on top) covers lamp 1 at about x 39.6–43.8 %, y 40.2–46.7 % of the stage;
  - lamp 2 covers lamp 1 at about x 56.0–59.0 %, y 30.7–46.7 %.
  
  Whether this overlap covers any of lamp 1's visible pixels is uncertain.
- **Suggested fix:** Check by clicking. If needed, trim the hit area with a `clip-path` polygon on `.lamp`.

**11. Low: parallax does work on every mouse move anywhere on the page**
- **Where:** `js/lamp-parallax.js:113-121`, `js/lamp-parallax.js:92-96`.
- **Finding:** A document-wide `pointermove` wakes a rAF tick that reads two bounding rects, even when the cursor is over the footer. It settles in one frame, so the cost is small.
- **Suggested fix:** In the handler, skip `wake()` when `atRest` and the pointer is outside the last known hero rect, which is already refreshed on scroll.

**12. Low: tests check less than PLAN §4 says**
- `tests/header.spec.js:43,48`: only `main` is checked for `inert`. PLAN says "the rest of the page"; the footer and skip link aren't checked.
- `tests/slider.spec.js:69-77`: the timer restart is tested only for "next". PLAN says prev, next and segment clicks restart the 3 s timer.
- `tests/lamps.spec.js:131-141`: "in view" is checked only horizontally; there's no `b.y + b.height <= 812` check.
- `tests/reduced-motion.spec.js:11-17`: `movingAnimations` only looks at CSS transitions, not keyframe animations. The hint is also hidden by default (`tests/helpers.js:5-13`), so removing `hint-pulse` under reduced motion is never tested.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the missing assertions; none of them needs a snapshot or a threshold change.

**13. Low: PLAN.md is out of date (the code looks right in each case)**
- PLAN §1 lists `js/menu.js`; the menu lives in `js/header.js`.
- PLAN §3.1 has `--gutter: clamp(16px, 8.33vw, 160px)`; `tokens.css:83` has `16px`, which is consistent with PLAN §3.2.
- PLAN §3.3 describes centring with `translateX(calc(-50% + var(--stage-x)))`; `hero.css:66-73` uses `top/left: 50%` + `translate(-50%, -50%)`.
- The PLAN §2 `imagesizes` text has no contained-mode entry.
- **Suggested fix:** Update PLAN.md.

**14. Low: dead code**
- `tokens.css:27-28`: `--c-light-amber` and `--c-light-ember` are unused (see finding 1).
- `js/shader.js:147`: the `data-render-scale` override is never used by the markup or the tests.
- `css/hero.css:269-271` (`.hero__pause[hidden]`) and `css/lamps.css:319-321` (`.hero__hint[hidden]`) repeat `base.css:87-89` (`[hidden] { display: none !important }`).
- **Suggested fix:** Remove them, or keep `data-render-scale` with a test that uses it.

---

### Checked and found fine
- **Paths and loading:** only relative paths (no leading `/` in any href, src, srcset or `url()`); classic `<script defer>`, no modules, every script an IIFE with a `DOMContentLoaded` guard; works over file:// (no font preload, `localStorage` in try/catch).
- **Copy and controls:** every link is `href="#"`; the search form's `submit` is prevented (`header.js:13-18`).
- **Class names and hooks:** BEM names throughout (Stylelint pattern too); JS hooks are all `data-*`, and classes are only toggled for state.
- **Motion:**
  - one easing token, with `--ease-out` only for scale-ups and zoom;
  - only `transform`, `scale`, `translate` and `opacity` animate, plus the header `color` exception and discrete `visibility`;
  - hover rules sit inside `(hover: hover)` (apart from finding 3);
  - reduced motion is handled: tokens neutralise scale and movement, there's no autoplay, the pause button is hidden, the shader draws one frame, parallax is off, the flicker becomes a fade and the panel only fades.
- **JS lifecycle:**
  - The slider, shader and parallax rAF loops all stop: on pause, on hidden tab or off-screen, or once settled.
  - The slider clamps time gaps; the progress bar and the slide change share one clock.
  - Shader: context lost/restored, no-WebGL fallback, debounced ResizeObserver, 60 fps cap.
  - Null checks for every queried element. One exception, harmless in this markup: `hero-slider.js` assumes prev/next exist whenever there are 2+ slides.
- **Accessibility:**
  - Burger: `aria-expanded`, everything outside the header `inert`, focus trap, Esc returns focus, closes when widening past 1280.
  - Slider ARIA: roledescription, "1 z 2" labels, `aria-hidden` on the inactive slide, `aria-current` on the active segment, pause button `aria-pressed`.
  - Lamps: `aria-pressed` with a constant label; the hint is `aria-hidden`; the easter-egg copy is hidden from assistive tech via `content: … / ''`.
  - A visible two-tone focus ring on both light and dark backgrounds; alt text on content images and `alt=""` on decorative ones; real buttons for every control.
- **Images:** tile `srcset`/`sizes` match PLAN §3.6; `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"` on everything below the fold; hero slide 1 has `fetchpriority="high"` and its `sizes` match the preload `imagesizes` exactly.
- **Layout and performance:** the hero stage height comes only from `aspect-ratio`, as PLAN requires; `will-change` is set only while the parallax moves.
- **Tests:** the suite maps to criteria 1–11, and the assertions check what they claim (e.g. the reduced-motion burger test does catch a slide transition). No snapshots or loosened thresholds.
- **Dependencies:** `package.json` devDependencies match the list in CLAUDE.md.

The class goes at rest, and so do the extra layers.

  - above it, the slide's sky colour (sampled from the photo's top edge: rock `#9c6744`, unchanged in the clean photo, interior `#c5afa3`) fills the hero, and the stage image fades in over its top 25 %;
  - slide 2 adds a 45 % dark scrim behind the text, since white on `#c5afa3` is only about 2.1:1;
  - the text sits at the top under the header; its bottom padding reserves the stage height, so the hero grows instead of overlapping on short screens.

- Hero text: eyebrow "Bestsellery SOLLUX", H1 "Kolor i forma" / "w nowym świetle" (two lines, line break kept at desktop), yellow pill CTA "Sprawdź bestsellery". _(verified against #3, nodes 1:510, 1:511, 1:513)_
35:- **Tile text contrast.** White text on THORO's photo (about 1.4:1 at worst) and on Konfigurator's blue `#72a3f3` (2.55:1) is under WCAG minimums. The design colours stay; a dark gradient (`#101011`) sits behind the text block only, fading in above the eyebrow. Strength is the measured minimum plus 2 points: THORO 52 %, Konfigurator 32 %. Here's the merged list from both passes. Nothing has been fixed yet.

**How it ran:** I created `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` (tools: Read, Grep, Glob). This session only loaded the new agent type after the review had started. So I ran a fresh general-purpose agent with that file's exact instructions, limited to Read, Grep and Glob. The `reviewer` type now works for future runs. I spot-checked its main claims (header.js:66, the unused tokens, `data-render-scale`, the slide 2 scrim scope in PLAN §3.3) and they hold. Also, PLAN.md has no "stage 6", so I worked from your brief.

## Recommend fixing now

| # | Finding | Source | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hard-coded colours outside `tokens.css`: light-gradient stops in `lamps.css` (150, 236–238, 265–267, 281–283, 381–382), sky colours `hero.css:54,59`, black-with-alpha in `hero.css:316`, `tiles.css:96–97`, `shader.css:19`. `--c-light-amber` and `--c-light-ember` are unused but their values are typed by hand at `lamps.css:281–282`. | reviewer (high) | **Fix.** Move them to tokens; use `color-mix()` for the alpha variants. Should look identical; I'd confirm with before/after screenshots. |
| 2 | Hard-coded durations: hint delay `1.2s` (`lamps.css:316`), pulse `1.6s` (`lamps.css:337`). | reviewer (high) | **Fix** with two tokens. **Skip** `SMOOTH_MS = 160` in `lamp-parallax.js`: it sets how quickly the lamps catch up with the cursor, not a transition, so a comment is enough. |
| 3 | Hover with no `:focus-visible` equivalent: hero arrow overlay (`hero.css:199–203`), footer link underline (`footer.css:34–39`). | reviewer (high) | **Fix.** Two small rules, as the rest of the page already does. |
| 4 | Easter-egg glow fades with `--dur-zoom` (`lamps.css:386`), which is 0 ms under reduced motion, so an allowed fade snaps instead. | reviewer | **Fix:** use `--dur-fade`. |
| 5 | Hero `sizes` and the preload `imagesizes` use `100vh` and ignore the 560–1080 px height clamp (`index.html:24, 249, 276`). Example: 924 px requested vs a real ~995 px stage at 800 × 520. | reviewer | **Fix:** `calc(clamp(560px, 100svh, 1080px) * 1.7778)`, identical in all three so the preload is still reused. |
| 6 | Following a link in the burger panel closes it but leaves focus on a now-hidden link (`header.js:66–68`). | reviewer | **Fix:** `close(true)`, so focus returns to the burger. |
| 7 | The first-visit hint dot pulses forever (`lamps.css:337`), which may fall under WCAG 2.2.2 (motion over 5 s). | reviewer | **Fix:** stop after 3 pulses, about 6 s including the delay. |
| 8 | Tests check less than PLAN §4 claims: `inert` only on `main`; timer restart only tested for "next"; lamps "in view" at 375 only checked horizontally; reduced motion never checks keyframe animations or the hint pulse. | reviewer | **Fix:** add the assertions. No threshold or snapshot changes. |
| 9 | PLAN.md out of date: `js/menu.js` (it's `header.js`), the old `--gutter` clamp, the old stage centring, `imagesizes` missing the portrait-mode entry. | reviewer | **Fix** the docs. The code is right in each case. |
| 10 | Dead code: the unused light tokens, `.hero__pause[hidden]` and `.hero__hint[hidden]` (the base `[hidden]` rule already covers them), the unused `data-render-scale` override in `shader.js:147`. | reviewer | **Fix:** remove all three. |

## Measure first, then decide

| # | Finding | Source | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | On landscape screens, slide 2 has no scrim. PLAN gives white on `#c5afa3` as about 2.1:1, and the scrim only exists on portrait screens. Header links, eyebrow, H1 and badge sit straight on the interior photo. | reviewer (uncertain) | **Measure** at 1280 and 1920 the way the tile scrims were measured. If it's under 4.5:1, add a text-side scrim like `.tile--scrim`. axe can't catch text on photos. |
| 12 | The lamp switch-on flicker has about 3 opacity peaks in 450 ms. That's over 3 flashes per second; whether it breaks WCAG 2.3.1 depends on how large and bright the glow is. | reviewer (uncertain) | **Measure** the lit area at 1920. If it's near the limit, cut the flicker to one dip. That changes the look you approved, so it's your call. |
| 13 | Lamp buttons are full image rectangles: lamps 2 and 3 overlap lamp 1's box. | reviewer (uncertain) | **Check by clicking** lamp 1's visible edges. Only if a click goes to the wrong lamp, trim the hit areas with `clip-path`. |

## Recommend skipping or deferring

| # | Finding | Source | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | No favicon; on GitHub Pages `/favicon.ico` returns 404. | reviewer | **Defer** to the planned §3.9 polish pass, before the deploy. |
| 15 | Parallax wakes up on every mouse move anywhere on the page (`lamp-parallax.js:113–121`). | reviewer | **Skip.** It settles in one frame, and frame time was measured as unchanged. |
| 16 | No `<link rel="preload" as="font">`. | guidelines | **Skip.** You decided this: it breaks file://, and Lighthouse will check the font timing. |

/* Hit area: the image boxes overlap (lamps 2 and 3 sit over lamp 1's box),
   so the button itself takes no pointer events and its image does, clipped to
   the convex hull of its visible pixels. Clicks bubble from the image to the
   button; the focus ring stays on the unclipped button. The hulls enclose
   every pixel with alpha > 0 (computed from the lamp PNGs on a 60 x 60 grid,
   rounded outward), so nothing visible changes. tests/lamps.spec.js checks
   that lamp 1's visible pixels next to lamps 2 and 3 click lamp 1. */
.lamp {
  position: absolute;
  top: var(--y);
  left: var(--x);
  width: var(--w);
  pointer-events: none;
}

.lamp__img {
  width: 100%;

content.content:
- In the panel the account icon shows its label "Moje konto" (on desktop the label is visually hidden and is the link's accessible name), and both panel icons are 24 px so the labels line up.
- Sizes and spacing: §0.3. The header row uses 16 px side padding with a max width of 1600 (as in Figma), not a wider page gutter. Group gaps `clamp(16px, 3.33vw, 64px)`, link gaps `clamp(12px, 1.67vw, 32px)`; the search pill takes the remaining width. From 1280 to 1439 the configurator is icon-only (label kept for screen readers). Measured search width: 270 px at 1280–1439, 374 px at 1920.

### 3.3 Hero stage (`.hero`, `.hero__stage`)

- `.hero` uses `--hero-h: clamp(560px, 100svh, 1080px)`, with `height: var(--hero-h)`, `overflow: hidden` and `position: relative`. `svh`, not `vh`, so the hero doesn't jump when the mobile browser bar shows or hides.
- `.hero__stage` has `aspect-ratio: 1920 / 1080` and covers the hero like `object-fit: cover`:
  - `width: max(100%, var(--hero-h) * 16 / 9)`; the height comes **only** from `aspect-ratio`. Never derive it as `calc(var(--stage-w) * 9 / 16)`: inside `height` the `100%` resolves against the hero's height, which squashed the photo on viewports wider than 16:9 (bug found at 1280 × 633, fixed);
  - centred with `left: 50%; transform: translateX(calc(-50% + var(--stage-x, 0%)))`.
- Inside the stage, all absolutely positioned in % of the stage:
  - `.hero__slide` ×2 (`hero-rock-clean`, `hero-interior`), stacked. Neither photo has lamps in it: slide 1 uses `hero-rock-clean.png`, the rock photo with the lamps removed (user-made in Figma, see NOTES.md);
  - `.hero__stage--lamps` above both slides, containing three `<button class="lamp lamp--N" aria-pressed>` elements, each holding its lamp image. The light lives in separate layers (below).
- **Lamp positions:** left/top/width in % of the stage, taken from `design/lamp-positions.json` (§0.2). They aren't from Figma; the lamps aren't in the hero frame. For reference, the PNGs at 2× are 744×838, 940×856, 846×786, which is 372×419, 470×428, 423×393 at 1920, if the match confirms scale 1.0.
- **Both slides:** the lamp images are always visible and never fade or zoom; only the backgrounds crossfade and zoom underneath them. (Earlier the lamps were baked into the rock photo and the overlays were handed off by opacity, which showed the lamps twice during transitions: a dip mid-crossfade on 1 → 2, and the baked lamps zooming into the overlays on 2 → 1.)
- **Lamp light on click (built, option B with a light dim; user-approved; `css/lamps.css`, `js/lamps.js`):**
  - Layers, bottom to top: slides → lamps → `.hero__dim` → `.hero__stage--light` (screen blend) → text. Per lamp, `.light--N` holds a hover/focus glow (`.light__peek`) and the light group (`.light__glow`: diffuser disc, halo, cone, pool on the rock). Geometry is in % of the 1920:1080 stage, read from the lamp PNGs, so it scales at every width.
  - Switching on: a 450 ms opacity flicker, then steady; off: a 300 ms fade. Reduced motion: a plain 600 ms fade both ways, no flicker.
  - Room dim deepens per lamp: `--lamp-dim-1/2/3` = 0.06 / 0.11 / 0.15 in `tokens.css` (tunable). With no lamp on the dim is 0 and the light layer is `visibility: hidden` (a blended layer switches nearby text to greyscale anti-aliasing), so the hero is pixel-identical to before (verified: 0 differing pixels, also after switching a lamp on and off).
  - Slide 2: diffuser glow and cones work the same; the pools fade out with the crossfade (there's no rock), keyed on the active slide in CSS.
  - Discoverability: pointer cursor; faint diffuser glow on hover and keyboard focus; first-visit pill "Kliknij lampę" next to lamp 2 (under it in the portrait layout), hidden after the first click and remembered in `localStorage` (try/catch). The pill is `aria-hidden`; the buttons already say "Włącz lampę 1–3".
  - Easter egg: all three on → "w nowym świetle" glows warm (a copy of the words fades in on top; its generated text is hidden from assistive tech with `content: attr(data-text) / ""`).
  - Motion rules: only opacity animates (the light groups, the peek, the dim, the headline glow); the blurred / clipped shapes are static and the blend sits on a layer that never animates.

**Outcome:** "Pn–Pt 7:00–15:00"; at 375 the line now fits on one row. Recorded in NOTES.md and README as a copy change.

**Source:** guidelines

**Finding:** No text-wrap: balance on headings.

**Source:** guidelines

### 2. Hard-coded durations

**Finding:** Hard-coded durations: hint delay 1.2s (lamps.css:316), pulse 1.6s (lamps.css:337).

**Source:** reviewer (high)

**Finding:** Lamp buttons are full image rectangles: lamps 2 and 3 overlap lamp 1's box.

**Source:** reviewer (uncertain)

**Finding:** Easter-egg glow fades with --dur-zoom (lamps.css:386), which is 0 ms under reduced motion, so an allowed fade snaps instead.

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix: use --dur-fade.

### 5. Hero sizes and preload imagesizes

**Finding:** Hero sizes and the preload imagesizes use 100vh and ignore the 560–1080 px height clamp (index.html:24, 249, 276). Example: 924 px requested vs a real ~995 px stage at 800 × 520.

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix: calc(clamp(560px, 100svh, 1080px) * 1.7778), identical in all three so the preload is still reused.

### 6. Focus after following a burger menu link

**Finding:** Following a link in the burger panel closes it but leaves focus on a now-hidden link (header.js:66–68).

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix: close(true), so focus returns to the burger.

### 7. First-visit hint dot animation

**Finding:** The first-visit hint dot pulses forever (lamps.css:337), which may fall under WCAG 2.2.2 (motion over 5 s).

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix: stop after 3 pulses, about 6 s including the delay.

### 8. Test coverage gaps

**Finding:** Tests check less than PLAN §4 claims: inert only on main; timer restart only tested for "next"; lamps "in view" at 375 only checked horizontally; reduced motion never checks keyframe animations or the hint pulse.

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix: add the assertions. No threshold or snapshot changes.

### 9. Outdated PLAN.md

**Finding:** PLAN.md out of date: js/menu.js (it's header.js), the old --gutter clamp, the old stage centring, imagesizes missing the portrait-mode entry.

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix the docs. The code is right in each case.

### 10. Dead code

**Finding:** Dead code: the unused light tokens, .hero__pause[hidden] and .hero__hint[hidden] (the base [hidden] rule already covers them), the unused data-render-scale override in shader.js:147.

**Source:** reviewer

**Recommendation:** Fix: remove all three.

**Finding:** Parallax wakes up on every mouse move anywhere on the page (lamp-parallax.js:113–121).

The text shadow and the slide 1 scrim are in and committed. They fix the slide 1 eyebrow, but the two places where text crosses a lamp still don't reach the WCAG ratios. The polish pass (favicon and final checks) is also done and committed. Nothing is pushed.

**What changed:**
- **Text shadow:** a tight 2 px dark halo plus a soft 12 px one. It's on the eyebrow, the H1 and, from 1280 px, the header links, configurator and search text. It disappears as soon as the header turns white (hover, focus, open menu), and no lamp is dimmed.
- **Slide 1 scrim:** a 30 % band behind the text column, under the lamps. The eyebrow needs 28 % at worst (1440 × 900), plus the 2 points.

**Before → after**, measured within 2 px of the letters (a text shadow only darkens there):

| Item | Need | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slide 1 eyebrow (1280 / 1920) | 4.5 | 2.85 / 2.78 | **5.16 / 5.04** |
| "świetle" over lamp 3 (both slides) | 3 | 1.53–1.75 | 2.02–2.07 |
| Nav over lamp 1 at 1280 × 633 | 4.5 | 1.58–1.63 | 1.80–1.84 |

**Your call: the two lamp overlaps.** No subtle shadow gets there; the nav needs about 47 % black right at the letter edges. I also tried a heavy stacked halo: "świetle" only passes within 1 px of the letters (3.21), the nav still doesn't (3.37), and it starts to look like an outline. I kept the subtle version, as you asked. The options:
- a stronger halo on the H1 only;
- for the nav, keeping lamp 1 below the header on screens wider than 16:9. That moves the photo stage instead of dimming anything.

**Also below the threshold on slide 1, as designed:** I found these while measuring and left them alone, because they weren't in your list:
- the search placeholder at 1280 is 3.74;
- the configurator label at 1920 is 4.31;
- the badge label on its dark pill is 3.60.

**Polish pass:**
- `favicon.svg` is the logo's "S", white on a black rounded square. A test checks it loads.
- html-validate, Stylelint and Prettier are clean, and 51 tests pass across three runs.
- By eye at 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1280 × 633, 1440 and 1920: nothing overlaps or gets cut off.
- Lighthouse is still pending the deploy.
